user_intent: Add useful, detailed multiplication/square builtin laws and proof compositions to the mathematics-first Manual, with exact signs, domains, equality cases and checked examples.
forward_derivation: Real ordered-field signs and nonzero conditions
Sign-preserving/reversing products, cancellation and factorwise bounds
Squares as magnitudes, root domains and zero/equality cases
Nonnegative polynomial/rational certificates for weighted and Cauchy bounds
Positive-denominator comparisons and completed quadratic lower bounds

recipes: R11 product signs, zero factors, cancellation and two varying factors
R12 squares, absolute values, root domains, zero/positive cases
R13 squared-sum/product bounds, weighted Young, two-dimensional Cauchy and equality cases
R14 clearing positive denominators and a general positive quadratic
publication.boundary_examples: Zero cancellation, unsigned square reflection, signed factorwise multiplication, selecting an unspecified zero factor, invalid negative weight and square-root sign.

distinction.native_direct: Native sign/nonzero/zero-product and square/absolute-value identities are exercised as bare universal facts. Weak two-factor monotonicity and square-to-magnitude order also verify directly.
distinction.composed: Cancellation, strict two-factor comparison, signed square reflection, weighted estimates, Cauchy certificates and denominator changes have explicit short proof routes. They are not new public builtin predicates or automatic tactics.
distinction.limits: No general finite Cauchy theorem or nonlinear optimization search is claimed. Failed optional AM-GM, absolute-product Young and reciprocal sketches were not promoted as checked examples.

native_bypasses: Zero-product elimination with a known nonzero factor
Two nonpositive factors give nonnegative product
required: Both explicit square-domain facts plus root chain for signed square reflection
removed: Separate square sign before weighted certificate
Separate square sign before positive quadratic product
Separate absolute-square identities before reverse magnitude-order chain
